sections.body: Real-time rendering systems can reduce cost by exploiting coherence across adjacent frames or across the human visual field instead of recomputing uniform full-quality results everywhere. Temporal coherence reuses previous-frame information when values remain stable, while foveated rendering allocates higher quality near the fovea and lower quality in the periphery under perceptual constraints.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: The shared concept is conditional reuse: both approaches depend on identifying where lower computation remains visually acceptable. Temporal methods emphasize stability across camera, lighting, time, and interaction changes; foveated methods emphasize human-visual-system models, regional quality differences, and integration into rendering paradigms.
sections.heading: Section 2

sections.body: The evidence is strongest for temporal rendering and foveated rendering. The connection to other rendering systems should be framed as an optimization pattern rather than a single unified algorithm.
sections.heading: Section 3

title: Temporal and Perceptual Quality Allocation in Real-Time Rendering
